MIMT 5010.title: Market Research for Business Applications
MIMT 5010.description: This course aims to investigate the market research process and its application as a problem-solving tool for management decision making. Methods, techniques, and procedures of market research will be discussed, including topics on defining research problems, designing a research project, and in collecting, analyzing, recording and interpreting data, and report writing and presentation.
cilos: Evaluate marketing research and identify the opportunities and potential limitations of it.
Identify the challenges and opportunities of executing a marketing research project in an international context.
Critically evaluate and analyze marketing research data.
Explain how new technological developments (big data, social media, mobile and physiological devices) may facilitate marketing research.
Design and implement a marketing research project to solve business problems.

MIMT 5020.title: Managerial Decision Making
MIMT 5020.description: High quality managerial decisions require quality decision content and quality decision making process. This course focuses on the concepts and techniques that can develop effective decision-making skills for those who will be in management positions, both as individuals and in teams. Emphasis of topics will be put on how to facilitate and formalize the decision-making process, reveal decision-making biases and enable decision analysis to work as a powerful and flexible management tool that can address many types of business problems. It helps students understand what traps might be involved in the decision-making process and what can be done to improve the quality of decisions as a manager.
cilos: Describe how human beings make decisions and identify the major errors and biases in thinking and judgment.
Increase the awareness of removing the obstacles in decision making.
Suggest some strategies to overcome the obstacles in decision making.
Apply decision making techniques and strategies in daily and managerial contexts.

MIMT 5110.title: Doing Business in Asia
MIMT 5110.description: The course is designed to allow students to appreciate and understand the opportunities and challenges in doing business in the Asian countries. The course provides a broad introduction to key issues in the business environment including business policy, corporate governance, legal aspects, strategy, marketing and branding, services management and cross-cultural management, etc.. The implications of political, socio-economic, and cultural environment provide students with insights into how to formulate and implement strategies for competitive advantage and value creation in Asia.
cilos: Integrate inter-disciplinary knowledge to comprehensively analyze China’s business environment at present and in the future.
Analyze business opportunities and threats in China.
Evaluate firms’ strategic decisions to do business in China.
Deliver a clearly written final write up based on comprehensive knowledge.

MIMT 5120.title: Strategic Management in Asia
MIMT 5120.description: The primary topic of this course is strategic management in the Asian context. It focuses on key theories and frameworks in strategic management, the characteristics of the specific business environment in Asia, and insights of how to apply these theories and frameworks into the Asian context. It helps students who plan to work in Asian companies understand their roles and responsibilities in helping the companies to achieve competitive advantage; and to help those who work in foreign companies that either already have or will have operations in Asia to obtain the knowledge necessary to compete or cooperate with Asian companies more successfully.
cilos: Apply the key concepts, frameworks and techniques for dealing with business challenges in a culturally diverse setting with a global perspective.
Evaluate business problems as a general manager from a general management perspective connected with the corporate world.
Develop creative thinking skills and ethics by integrating original, innovative, and ethical approaches to strategic problems.
Develop comprehensive leadership skills, particularly in the Asian context.

MIMT 5200.title: Global Citizenship: Responsible Citizenship and Global Sustainability
MIMT 5200.description: Global citizenship is the global exercise of ethical, values-based citizenship in the pursuit of economic and societal progress and sustainable development. It requires the vision and courage to place decision making and management practice in a global context. Nowadays, globally responsible managers at all organizational levels all over the world face ever-changing challenges and they are embedding global responsibility in their business to deal with these challenges. Topics in the course include understanding the global business environment, responsible management behaviours, corporate global responsibility and sustainable global business practices, etc..
cilos: Identify the role-related responsibilities and the basic principles of responsible decision-making and global stakeholder management.
Identify and analyze ethical and social dilemmas.
Generate solutions to business challenges involving complex social issues.
Identify the importance of responsible management in society.
Maintain a balanced view on stakeholder management and time perspectives.

MIMT 5200.title: Global Citizenship
MIMT 5200.description: Global citizenship is the global exercise of ethical, values-based citizenship in the pursuit of economic and societal progress and sustainable development. It requires the vision and courage to place decision making and management practice in a global context. Nowadays, globally responsible managers at all organizational levels all over the world face ever-changing challenges and they are embedding global responsibility in their business to deal with these challenges. Topics in the course include understanding the global business environment, responsible management behaviours, corporate global responsibility and sustainable global business practices, etc..
cilos: Identify the role-related responsibilities and the basic principles of responsible decision-making and global stakeholder management.
Identify and analyze ethical and social dilemmas.
Generate solutions to business challenges involving complex social issues.
Identify the importance of responsible management in society.
Maintain a balanced view on stakeholder management and time perspectives.

MIMT 5210.title: Managing Global Complexity
MIMT 5210.description: This course focuses on the challenges and opportunities associated with organizational management and business strategy in the global environment. It provides a managerial overview of how different countries' cultural, social, political, technological and economic environments affect the strategic, organizational, and human resource issues that affect multinational companies. Key topics include globalization, culture, cross-cultural communication, negotiation, motivation, leadership and group dynamics. It develops a managerial mindset to practice management, encourages students to move between management concepts and their real-life applicability and ultimately adapts to the ever-changing world of management practice.
cilos: Conduct business management exercises in a culturally diverse setting, particularly in the area of conflict management and dispute resolution.
Recognize, analyze, and manage disputes and conflicts in culturally diverse environments.
Apply advanced management principles developed from systematic analyses of cases and simulations.
Recognize ethical implications of different dispute resolution methods across contexts.
Solve problems and generate integrative solutions.

MIMT 5310.title: Understanding Consumers: A Strategic Approach
MIMT 5310.description: Consumers react to marketing information provided about a product. The topics discussed comprise an examination of basic psychological processes in a logical sequence: i.e., exposure, attention, perception, memory, persuasion, and decision-making. Advertising - and how consumers process ads -  is the major vehicle used to clarify these concepts. In addition, the course also furthers an understanding of consumer behavior by examining its social and cultural context, including the influence of group members (such as family and other important referents) on decision making and perception, and the nature and importance of cultural differences in consumer behaviour around the world. Thus, this course both a micro and macro perspective on the factors influencing a customer.
cilos: Evaluate consumers’ buying patterns and decisions using the concepts and theories of perception, learning, motivation, personality, lifestyle, and attitudes.
Assess and select appropriate market segments for targeting by applying the concepts of culture, demographics, opinion leadership, and other consumer behavioral dimensions.
Evaluate the effectiveness of marketing and advertising programs using relevant consumer behavior concepts and frameworks.
Make strategic and ethical marketing mix recommendations to enhance business performance based on the application of relevant consumer behavior concepts, frameworks and theories.

MIMT 5350.title: Project Management
MIMT 5350.description: This course covers the essential project management skills to ensure successful implementation of business projects. Topics include investment decisions, resource planning, budgeting, scheduling, outsourcing, and risk assessment and control, etc.
cilos: Analyze the core issues in project management and identify critical success factors.
Solve several project management problems with appropriate tools and techniques.
Compare and contrast different project management methodologies.
Identify the major project deliverables and when they are due.

MIMT 5410.title: Business and Climate Change in Asia Pacific
MIMT 5410.description: Climate change is the biggest challenge of today and tomorrow. Businesses contribute to climate change but also suffer from its consequences, while for selected industries it poses great opportunities. This course provides a comprehensive, interactive, and multi-disciplinary understanding of the threats, challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. The students could gain the competitive insights and tools required to be at the forefront of change.
cilos: Demonstrate a real-world understanding of the multifaceted business risks posed by climate change, and the strategic opportunities and untapped value that arise from taking action.
Identify and explain different developments in the region related to climate change and the possibilities to counteract it.
Summarize the diverging interests of parties involved in global climate policy negotiations, including governments, industry associations, global companies, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs).

Apply strategic tools for assessing the impact of climate change on firms, consumers and financial markets for developing successful corporate strategies to hedge against climate risk and embrace low-carbon business opportunities.
Implement consensus solutions, and experience the global dimension of the climate challenge.

MIMT 5450.title: Entrepreneurial Strategy for the Digital and Global Era
MIMT 5450.description: This curated course offers a window to the real-world entrepreneurial journey, using contemporary case studies, class and online discussions, and collaborative projects. These enable students to better grasp fundamental issues in entrepreneurship: addressing root causes of failure, identifying a winning Minimum Viable Product (MVP), attracting investors, and succeeding in platform and data-driven businesses. Students emerge equipped to launch or join new ventures or lead entrepreneurial initiatives within established organizations.
cilos: Understand and use key theoretical concepts in entrepreneurship and innovation from strategy and organizational perspectives.
Evaluate the interplay of start-ups, investors, governments, and other key players in today’s ecosystem.
Generate creative business ideas and evaluate their feasibility as entrepreneurial opportunities.
Communicate entrepreneurial ideas effectively to prospective investors and customers.
Assess the role of established corporations in driving innovation, and the interplay between them and new business ventures.
Identify the tradeoffs involving co-founders, hires, investors, and alliance partners in the start-up.

MIMT 5560.title: Management and Decision Making with Artificial Intelligence
MIMT 5560.description: In the rapidly evolving landscape of modern business, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a cornerstone technology driving strategic decision-making processes. This course is a comprehensive course designed to equip current and future leaders with the knowledge and skills necessary to leverage AI tools effectively in managerial contexts. Over this course, participants will dive into the fundamentals of AI, exploring how machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics can inform and enhance decision-making in various business domains. By the end of this course, participants will have a solid foundation in managing with AI, ready to harness its potential to transform decision-making and competitive strategies across multiple industries.
cilos: Identify opportunities where AI can add value to decision-making processes.
Evaluate the capabilities and limitations of current AI-based decision-making technologies.
Implement AI tools to analyze data, forecast trends, and make informed strategic decisions.
Navigate the ethical and societal implications of deploying AI-based decision-making technologies in business settings.
Cultivate a mindset of innovation and agility, preparing them to lead in a technology-driven future.

MIMT 5570.title: The Art and Science of Crisis Negotiation and Management
MIMT 5570.description: Conflict is an unavoidable human phenomenon. Wherever people interact, arising from different preferences and perspectives. Effective communication and negotiation skills are essential to navigate challenges and unlock positive outcomes. This course aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills and mindset to navigate, manage and resolve conflicts for themselves and others. Students will be introduced to concepts like active listening, the Behavioral Change Stairway Model and key strategies for managing challenging people and building collaboration. Through this course, students will undertake a journey of self-discovery, exploring their strengths and limitations in understanding themselves and others. Adopting a person-centered approach, the curriculum will focus on enhancing each student's innate motivation to change, turning moments of difficulty into opportunities for growth, understanding and positive transformation.
cilos: Understand the basic knowledge, attitude and skills in communication.
Acknowledge the importance of developing holistic wellness in preparing for daily challenges and crisis.
Identify and critique their own basic communication style, identifying areas of strength and areas for development.
Identify and demonstrate non-verbal behaviors and skills which indicate relationship attending.
Identify the occurrence of conflict, de-escalate the situation, and facilitate a collaborative and mutually beneficial resolution.
Demonstrate appropriate use of listening and communication skills in managing conflicts.
Apply active listening skills in crisis situations in the workplace.

MIMT 5580.title: Business Intelligence for Managers
MIMT 5580.description: Designed for students with limited prior analytics training, this course focuses on technology awareness, KPI design, dashboard interpretation, and data-informed managerial judgment rather than coding or advanced modeling. Students are introduced to the enterprise data stack, the managerial logic from descriptive to prescriptive analysis, and selected foundational methods as they support modern business intelligence (BI) and decision making. The course then extends classical BI toward more recent developments, including augmented analytics, generative AIdriven analytics, conversational BI, automated insight generation, and human-in-the-loop decision support. Upon completion of this course, students will develop a manager’s view of how data is transformed into insight, dashboards, decisions, and action.
cilos: Explain the data stack, BI terminology, and the logic of BI-driven decision-making.
Interpret dashboards, KPIs, alerts, and analytic outputs to diagnose business performance issues.
Evaluate the suitability and limits of foundational analytics methods for BI and decision support.
Formulate responsible recommendations that combine BI insights, human judgment, and automation.
Design a high-level BI roadmap for a business use case, including AI-enabled BI and humanoid-native enterprise opportunities.

MIMT 5780.title: Leveraging Personality in the Workplace
MIMT 5780.description: This course covers major psychological perspectives and current research on personality. It provides an in-depth examination of how personality theories can be applied to understanding personality in the workplace.
cilos: Recognize the major perspectives of personality psychology.
Demonstrate how to integrate different perspectives to analyze a subject.
Demonstrate the ability to read, summarize, interpret, and integrate information pertinent to personality-related topics.
Identify a research question, devise an action plan to conduct a study, gather and analyze the relevant information, and present the findings in a written report.

MIMT 6110.title: Skill Seminar I
MIMT 6110.description: This skill seminar will be offered to develop the students' essential business and communication skills necessary to work in a global business environment such as communication, teamwork, negotiation and presentation skills. Some possible skill seminars include topics on time management, inter-cultural skills, group work abilities, international negotiation techniques, presentation skills, to name a few.
cilos: Develop essential business communication skills for various business objectives in a global context.
Deliver well prepared and organized writing and presentation results.

MIMT 6120.title: Skill Seminar II
MIMT 6120.description: This skill seminar will be offered to develop the students' essential business and communication skills necessary to work in a global business environment such as communication, teamwork, negotiation and presentation skills. Some possible skill seminars include topics on time management, inter-cultural skills, group work abilities, international negotiation techniques, presentation skills, to name a few. Graded P or F.
cilos: Develop essential business communication skills for various business objectives in a global context.
Broaden international business prospects for various companies.
Discuss and interact with key managers from different firms.

MIMT 6200.title: Business Project
MIMT 6200.description: This is a supervised study of a real-life issued faced by an organization, including identification of strategic questions, design of studies, collection and analysis of data, development and reporting recommendation. Students will develop consultant-client relationship with the participating sponsoring companies and work in teams to conduct a strategically focused study which results in a comprehensive report containing analyses and practical recommendations for management decision making.
cilos: Create professional quality project deliverables including agendas, briefs, proposals, models and reports.
Manage a business project effectively.
Integrate disciplinary knowledge and apply appropriate analytical tools in formulating solutions to practical business problems in real world settings.
Deliver clear and engaging business presentations for a senior management audience.

MIMT 6300.title: International Internship
MIMT 6300.description: Students are required to work on a minimum of 10-week international internship to get practical work experience to prepare for graduate employment. The location of international internship together with students' home country, home school and exchange school must cover at least three countries. Students' performance in the internship will be assessed and evaluated by the company upon completion of the internship. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Solve management problems in a real global business environment by integrating various trainings from the program.
Deliver good performance with evaluations from corporations.
